questions.question: Which apostle is traditionally regarded as the first pope of the Catholic Church?
choices: A: Paul
B: Peter
C: James

questions.explanation: Peter is considered the first pope of the Catholic Church and is frequently mentioned in the Acts of the Apostles. He played a central role in the early Christian community and is seen as one of Jesus' closest disciples.

Which country is home to the capital city of Cairo?

questions.question: Cairo is the largest city in Egypt and also its capital. It is located on the Nile River and is known for its historical significance as well as its proximity to the Pyramids of Giza.
choices: B: Egypt
C: Sudan

What political system was established in the Roman Republic?

questions.question: The Roman Republic, which existed from around 509 BC to 27 BC, was a political system that included elements of democracy, particularly through elections and popular assemblies. During the Republic, citizens had the right to elect certain representatives, distinguishing it from a monarchy.
choices: B: Democracy
C: Oligarchy
D: Monarchy
Which famous opening sentence is from the novel 'Moby Dick' by Herman Melville?

questions.question: 'Call me Ishmael.' is the iconic opening sentence of 'Moby Dick,' published in 1851 and considered one of the most famous openings in world literature. The sentence is concise and introduces the narrator while alluding to his forthcoming adventure story.
choices: B: 'Call me Ishmael.'
C: 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.'
D: 'All happy families are alike.'

What is the origin of the English word 'salary'?

The word 'salary' is derived from the Latin word 'salarium,' which referred to the payments made to soldiers for the purchase of salt. This etymology highlights the historical importance of salt as a valuable commodity.

questions.question: A: Latin
choices: C: German
D: Slavic
